cannot branch on a ciphertext and cannot index an array by one. Those two facts      are why every confidential lottery published so far walks all N depositors: the only      oblivious construction available is \"compare the random point against every prefix sum\".      The way out is an observation about what the leak actually is. A tournament descent that      publicly reveals which child it took at each level reveals the winner's slot index one      digit at a time \u2014 and the winner's identity is published anyway. The path *is* the      answer. Revealing it early costs nothing, and it turns an O(N) scan into a descent over      `treeDepth` levels.      Scaling the random point is the other half. Division by a ciphertext does not exist, and      rejection sampling would leak a bit about the pool total on every retry. So the test          r / 2^32  <  prefix_j / total      is cross-multiplied into          r * total  <  prefix_j * 2^32          (in euint128)      exact, unbiased to one part in 2^32, no division, and no total ever revealed. Descending      needs no fresh randomness: the residual `R' = R - prefix_{j-1} * 2^32` is uniform on      `[0, w_j * 2^32)`, so the same test recurses against the child's own prefix sums. There is      one ciphertext-by-ciphertext multiply in the entire draw \u2014 the most expensive operation      available, spent exactly once, at the root.      **Why a level is two transactions.** The binding per-transaction ceiling is sequential      depth, not global compute, which is the opposite of what the sizing arithmetic suggested.      Sealing the k children is k independent chains and is depth-flat at every arity; the      selection that follows is 77% of the depth budget on its own. Measured together they      revert. Split, they fit \u2014 see `bench/RESULTS.md` and `deploy/params.ts`.      A draw is therefore `1 + 2 * treeDepth + 1` transactions: commit (which seals the root's      children), then select and reveal at each level, then settle. FHE.add(scan[i], scan[i - d]) : scan[i];\n            }\n            scan = next;\n        }\n\n        euint128 point = _point[id];\n\n        // The one ciphertext-by-ciphertext multiply in the whole draw, and only at the root.\n        // Below the root the point is already a residual on the same 2^32 scale.\n        if (draw.level == 0) {\n            point = FHE.mul(point, FHE.asEuint128(scan[k - 1]));\n            FHE.allowThis(point);\n            _point[id] = point;\n        }\n\n        euint8 idx = FHE.asEuint8(0);\n        for (uint32 i = 0; i + 1 < k; i++) {\n            ebool passed = FHE.ge(point, FHE.shl(FHE.asEuint128(scan[i]), uint8(32)));\n            idx = FHE.add(idx, FHE.asEuint8(passed));\n        }\n\n        FHE.allowThis(idx);\n        FHE.makePubliclyDecryptable(idx);\n        _index[id] = idx;\n        draw.phase = Phase.Selected;\n\n        emit LevelSelected(id, draw.level, euint8.unwrap(idx));\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Submit the KMS-signed decryption of the published index, descend into that child,\n    ///         and seal its children ready for the next level.\n    ///\n    /// @dev Two separate bindings have to hold and only one of them comes from the KMS.\n    ///      `FHE.checkSignatures` proves the cleartext belongs to *these handles in this order*;\n    ///      it says nothing about whether these handles are the ones this draw published. So the\n    ///      handle is compared against stored state first. Without that check a valid proof for\n    ///      any other publicly decryptable value would drive this draw wherever its holder liked.\n    ///\n    ///      The residual is computed here rather than at selection because the child index is\n    ///      plaintext by now \u2014 which is what lets the prefix be summed over a known range in a\n    ///      balanced tree, four operations deep instead of fifteen.\n    function revealLevel(uint256 id, bytes32[] calldata handles, uint8 child, bytes calldata proof) external {\n        Draw storage draw = _mustBe(id, Phase.Selected);\n        if (handles.length != 1 || handles[0] != euint8.unwrap(_index[id])) revert UnknownHandle();\n        if (child >= arity) revert ChildOutOfRange(child);\n\n        FHE.checkSignatures(handles, abi.encode(child), proof);\n\n        if (child > 0) {\n            euint64 consumed = _sumRange(_children[id], 0, child);\n            euint128 point = FHE.sub(_point[id], FHE.shl(FHE.asEuint128(consumed), uint8(32)));\n            FHE.allowThis(point);\n            _point[id] = point;\n        }\n\n        uint32 node = childOf(draw.node, child);\n        draw.node = node;\n        draw.level += 1;\n        _index[id] = euint8.wrap(bytes32(0));\n\n        emit LevelRevealed(id, draw.level - 1, child, node);\n\n        if (draw.level == treeDepth) {\n            draw.leafReached = true;\n            draw.phase = Phase.Prepared;\n            uint32 slot = node - leafOffset;\n            draw.winnerSlot = slot;\n            draw.winner = depositorAt[slot];\n        } else {\n            draw.phase = Phase.Prepared;\n            _prepare(id, draw);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Sum `values[from..to)` as a balanced tree, so depth is log2 of the range rather than\n    ///      the length of it. The range is plaintext, so this is ordinary arithmetic on handles.\n    function _sumRange(euint64[] storage values, uint32 from, uint32 to) private returns (euint64) {\n        uint32 n = to - from;\n        euint64[] memory level = new euint64[](n);\n        for (uint32 i = 0; i < n; i++) level[i] = values[from + i];\n\n        while (n > 1) {\n            uint32 half = (n + 1) / 2;\n            euint64[] memory next = new euint64[](half);\n            for (uint32 i = 0; i < half; i++) {\n                uint32 a = 2 * i;\n                next[i] = a + 1 < n ? FHE.add(level[a], level[a + 1]) : level[a];\n            }\n            level = next;\n            n = half;\n        }\n        return level[0];\n    }\n\n    // ----------------------------------------------------------------- settle\n\n    /// @notice Pay the winner, release the tree, and execute everything that arrived mid-draw.\n    ///\n    /// @dev A draw that lands on an unoccupied leaf means the pool's total weight was zero \u2014 every\n    ///      depositor had withdrawn before the seal. There is no way to detect that under\n    ///      encryption and no reason to pretend otherwise: the prize goes back to the sponsor and\n    ///      the event records a winner of `address(0)`.\n    function settle(uint256 id) external {\n        Draw storage draw = _mustBe(id, Phase.Prepared);\n        if (!draw.leafReached) revert DrawNotFinished(id, draw.level, treeDepth);\n\n        draw.phase = Phase.Settled;\n        openDraw = 0;\n\n        address winner = draw.winner;\n        if (draw.prize > 0) {\n            euint64 prize = FHE.asEuint64(draw.prize);\n            FHE.allowThis(prize);\n            FHE.allowTransient(prize, address(token));\n            if (winner == address(0)) {\n                token.confidentialTransfer(draw.sponsor, prize);\n                emit PrizeReturned(id, draw.sponsor, draw.prize);\n            } else {\n                token.confidentialTransfer(winner, prize);\n            }\n        }\n\n        emit DrawSettled(id, winner, draw.winnerSlot, draw.prize, nextSlot);\n\n        _drainQueue();\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Release a draw that has stopped making progress, and give the prize back.\n    ///\n    /// @dev Deliberately callable by anyone and deliberately not a keeper privilege. The failure\n    ///      this exists for is the keeper going away, so a rescue only the keeper can perform is\n    ///      not a rescue. It cannot be used to cancel a draw that is merely slow: the window is\n    ///      six hours and a draw takes minutes.\n    ///\n    ///      No winner is paid and none is invented. The draw is recorded as abandoned at whatever\n    ///      level it reached, which is a fact worth keeping on a page that claims verifiability.\n    function abandonDraw(uint256 id) external {\n        if (id == 0 || id > drawCount) revert NoDraw(id);\n        Draw storage draw = _draws[id];\n        if (draw.phase == Phase.None || draw.phase == Phase.Settled) {\n            revert WrongPhase(id, Phase.Prepared, draw.phase);\n        }\n\n        uint32 expiresAt = draw.sealTime + DRAW_TIMEOUT;\n        if (block.timestamp < expiresAt) revert NotTimedOut(id, expiresAt);\n\n        draw.phase = Phase.Settled;\n        draw.winner = address(0);\n        openDraw = 0;\n\n        if (draw.prize > 0) {\n            euint64 prize = FHE.asEuint64(draw.prize);\n            FHE.allowThis(prize);\n            FHE.allowTransient(prize, address(token));\n            token.confidentialTransfer(draw.sponsor, prize);\n            emit PrizeReturned(id, draw.sponsor, draw.prize);\n        }\n\n        emit DrawAbandoned(id, draw.level, msg.sender);\n\n        _drainQueue();\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------- internals\n\n    function _mustBe(uint256 id, Phase expected) private view returns (Draw storage draw) {\n        if (id == 0 || id > drawCount) revert NoDraw(id);\n        draw = _draws[id];\n        if (draw.phase != expected) revert WrongPhase(id, expected, draw.phase);\n    }\n}\n","keccak256":"0xec9d82ebd5b41f728b1aba57439b086c91a0b5f5055f40f785b4517544f7d6b4","license":"MIT"},"contracts/Limits.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.27;\n\n/// @notice The three caps that keep the encrypted time-weighted integral inside `euint64`.\n///\n/// @dev FHE arithmetic wraps silently \u2014 there is no revert-on-overflow and there cannot be one,\n///      because detecting it would mean branching on a ciphertext. Every bound below is therefore\n///      enforced before a value can enter an aggregate: the plaintext ones with `require`, the\n///      encrypted one by clamping with `FHE.min`.\n///\n///      The arithmetic they protect:\n///\n///        B  = sum of balances                        <= MAX_DEPOSIT * MAX_SLOTS = 2^44\n///        dt = seconds since the aggregate last moved <= MAX_PERIOD              = 2^19\n///        weight = A + B*dt, and A + B*dt is the integral of balance over one period,\n///        so it is bounded by B * MAX_PERIOD                                     = 2^63\n///\n///      2^63 sits one bit under the `euint64` ceiling. That last bit is the margin, and it is the\n///      reason these are constants in a shared file rather than three numbers chosen locally.\nlibrary Limits {\n    /// @dev 2^32 base units. At 6 decimals that is ~4.29 million tokens in a single deposit.\n    uint64 internal constant MAX_DEPOSIT = 4_294_967_296;\n\n    /// @dev 2^12 slots. One slot per depositor, assigned on first deposit and never reused.\n    uint32 internal constant MAX_SLOTS = 4096;\n\n    /// @dev 2^19 seconds, ~6.1 days. A draw period may not be longer.\n    uint32 internal constant MAX_PERIOD = 524_288;\n}\n","keccak256":"0x5b01b6706f379c7a81d733b7ace6e8b601c2106b61b2a6deec94e8946f81a203","license":"MIT"},"contracts/TicketPool.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.27;\n\nimport {FHE, euint64, externalEuint64} from \"@fhevm/solidity/lib/FHE.sol\";\nimport {IERC7984} from \"@openzeppelin/confidential-contracts/interfaces/IERC7984.sol\";\n\nimport {Limits} from \"./Limits.sol\";\nimport {WeightTree} from \"./WeightTree.sol\";\n\n/// @notice Deposits and withdrawals over the encrypted weight tree.\n///\n/// @dev Principal is never at risk here and never earns a discount: a withdrawal returns exactly\n///      what was put in, and the only thing a deposit buys is time-weighted odds. The draw itself\n///      lives in `DrawMachine`; this contract owns the money and the tree.\n///\n///      The token is a constructor argument typed as `IERC7984`, so the demo's faucet token and a\n///      real confidential USDT are the same deployment with a different address.\ncontract TicketPool is WeightTree {\n    /// @notice The confidential asset depositors hold.\n    IERC7984 public immutable token;\n\n    /// @notice When period 0 began.\n    uint32 public immutable genesis;\n\n    /// @notice Seconds per draw period.\n    uint32 public immutable periodLength;\n\n    /// @notice Slot 0 is a real slot, so occupancy is tracked separately rather than by `slot != 0`.\n    mapping(address depositor => uint32 slot) private _slotOf;\n    mapping(address depositor => bool assigned) private _hasSlot;\n    mapping(uint32 slot => address depositor) public depositorAt;\n\n    /// @dev The last weight each depositor sealed for themselves. Written by `sealWeight`, read\n    ///      by nobody else \u2014 a weight is as private as the balance it is computed from.\n    mapping(address account => euint64 weight) private _sealedWeight;\n\n    /// @notice Slots are assigned once and never reused, so this only ever climbs.\n    uint32 public nextSlot;\n\n    /// @notice An interaction that arrived while a draw held the tree still, waiting to be\n    ///         executed the moment the draw settles.\n    ///\n    /// @dev `payTo` is zero for a deposit \u2014 the token already moved when it was queued \u2014 and the\n    ///      depositor for a withdrawal, whose token movement is what is being deferred.\n    struct Pending {\n        uint32 slot;\n        bool subtract;\n        address payTo;\n        euint64 amount;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The cap on interactions parked behind one draw. A draw is eight transactions and\n    ///         well under a minute, so this is a very deep queue in practice.\n    uint256 internal constant MAX_QUEUE = 32;\n\n    /// @notice Parked interactions executed per transaction.\n    ///\n    /// @dev Each one is a full leaf-to-root walk, so draining a full queue inside `settle` would\n    ///      need far more than a block will take. The drain is paged instead: `settle` does the\n    ///      first page and anyone may push the rest through. Settling is not allowed to depend on\n    ///      how many people happened to act while the draw was running.\n    ///\n    ///      Three, from the live measurement rather than the mock's. On Sepolia a deposit costs\n    ///      1,372,609 gas and 3,561,480 HCU \u2014 two and a half times what the mock priced it at \u2014\n    ///      so four would sit at 71% of the 20M compute ceiling before the payout is added, and a\n    ///      page that reverts under load is worse than a page that is one shorter.\n    ///      See `bench/LIVE.md`.\n    uint256 internal constant DRAIN_PER_TX = 3;\n\n    Pending[] private _queue;\n\n    /// @dev Read index into `_queue`. The array is cleared once it is fully drained rather than\n    ///      element by element, so this is what says where the drain has got to.\n    uint256 private _drained;\n\n    mapping(uint32 slot => bool queued) private _slotQueued;\n\n    error PoolFull();\n    error NoSlot(address account);\n    error PeriodTooLong(uint32 periodLength);\n    error PeriodZero();\n    error QueueFull();\n    error AlreadyQueued(uint32 slot);\n    error QueueNotDrained(uint256 remaining);\n\n    event SlotAssigned(address indexed depositor, uint32 indexed slot);\n    event Deposited(address indexed depositor, uint32 indexed slot);\n    event Withdrawn(address indexed depositor, uint32 indexed slot);\n    event WeightSealed(address indexed depositor, uint32 indexed slot, uint32 at);\n    event Queued(address indexed depositor, uint32 indexed slot, bool subtract, uint256 position);\n    event QueueDrained(uint256 count);\n\n    constructor(\n        IERC7984 token_,\n        uint32 arity_,\n        uint32 capacity_,\n        uint32 periodLength_\n    ) WeightTree(arity_, capacity_) {\n        if (periodLength_ == 0) revert PeriodZero();\n        if (periodLength_ > Limits.MAX_PERIOD) revert PeriodTooLong(periodLength_);\n\n        token = token_;\n        periodLength = periodLength_;\n        genesis = uint32(block.timestamp);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- periods\n\n    /// @notice The period `block.timestamp` falls in.\n    function currentPeriod() public view returns (uint32) {\n        return (uint32(block.timestamp) - genesis) / periodLength;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice When a period began.\n    function periodStart(uint32 period) public view returns (uint32) {\n        return genesis + period * periodLength;\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ slots\n\n    /// @notice The caller's slot, and whether they have one at all.\n    function slotOf(address account) public view returns (uint32 slot, bool assigned) {\n        return (_slotOf[account], _hasSlot[account]);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Depositors who have ever deposited. The draw descends over `capacity` leaves\n    ///         regardless, so this is a UX number, not a cost.\n    function participantCount() external view returns (uint32) {\n        return nextSlot;\n    }\n\n    function _slotFor(address account) private returns (uint32) {\n        if (_hasSlot[account]) return _slotOf[account];\n        if (nextSlot >= capacity) revert PoolFull();\n\n        uint32 slot = nextSlot++;\n        _slotOf[account] = slot;\n        _hasSlot[account] = true;\n        depositorAt[slot] = account;\n\n        emit SlotAssigned(account, slot);\n        return slot;\n    }\n\n    // --------------------------------------------------------------- deposits\n\n    /// @notice Deposit an encrypted amount. The caller must have made this contract an operator\n    ///         on the token first.\n    ///\n    /// @dev The amount is clamped twice and neither clamp can revert, because reverting on an\n    ///      encrypted comparison would leak the comparison. `FHE.min` caps it at `MAX_DEPOSIT` so\n    ///      the aggregates cannot overflow, and the token itself caps it at the sender's balance\n    ///      and returns what actually moved. That return value, not the request, is what enters\n    ///      the tree \u2014 otherwise a depositor could claim odds on money they never sent.\n    function deposit(externalEuint64 encryptedAmount, bytes calldata inputProof) external {\n        uint32 slot = _slotFor(msg.sender);\n\n        euint64 requested = FHE.fromExternal(encryptedAmount, inputProof);\n        euint64 capped = FHE.min(requested, FHE.asEuint64(Limits.MAX_DEPOSIT));\n        FHE.allowTransient(capped, address(token));\n\n        euint64 transferred = token.confidentialTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), capped);\n        FHE.allowThis(transferred);\n\n        _applyOrQueue(slot, transferred, false, address(0));\n        _grantLeaf(slot, msg.sender);\n\n        emit Deposited(msg.sender, slot);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------ withdrawals\n\n    /// @notice Withdraw an encrypted amount, clamped to the caller's balance.\n    ///\n    /// @dev Asking for more than you hold is not an error and must not be one: an error is a\n    ///      public signal about a private balance. The request is silently clamped, which is both\n    ///      the safe behaviour and the honest one \u2014 you cannot underflow the tree by guessing.\n    function withdraw(externalEuint64 encryptedAmount, bytes calldata inputProof) external {\n        uint32 slot = _requireSlot(msg.sender);\n        euint64 requested = FHE.fromExternal(encryptedAmount, inputProof);\n        (euint64 balance, ) = _balanceOf(slot);\n        _exit(slot, FHE.min(requested, balance));\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Withdraw the caller's entire principal.\n    function withdrawAll() external {\n        uint32 slot = _requireSlot(msg.sender);\n        (euint64 balance, ) = _balanceOf(slot);\n        _exit(slot, balance);\n    }\n\n    function _exit(uint32 slot, euint64 amount) private {\n        FHE.allowThis(amount);\n        _applyOrQueue(slot, amount, true, msg.sender);\n        _grantLeaf(slot, msg.sender);\n\n        emit Withdrawn(msg.sender, slot);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- queueing\n\n    /// @notice Whether a draw is currently holding the tree still. Always false here; the draw\n    ///         machine that inherits this contract is what makes it true.\n    function drawInFlight() public view virtual returns (bool) {\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice How many interactions are still waiting to be executed.\n    function queueLength() public view returns (uint256) {\n        return _queue.length - _drained;\n    }\n\n    /// @dev A draw is judged against the tree as it stood at its seal time, so the tree cannot\n    ///      move while one is in flight. Blocking withdrawals for that window would breach the\n    ///      promise that money is available at any time \u2014 the whole reason prize-linked saving is\n    ///      not gambling \u2014 so interactions are parked instead and executed automatically when the\n    ///      draw settles. The depositor acts once and the transaction lands without them.\n    ///\n    ///      One parked interaction per slot. A second withdrawal would clamp against a balance the\n    ///      first has not yet spent, and two of them together could ask for more than the leaf\n    ///      holds. The bound is on the slot, which is public, so refusing leaks nothing.\n    function _applyOrQueue(uint32 slot, euint64 amount, bool subtract, address payTo) internal {\n        if (!drawInFlight()) {\n            _execute(slot, amount, subtract, payTo);\n            return;\n        }\n\n        if (queueLength() >= MAX_QUEUE) revert QueueFull();\n        if (_slotQueued[slot]) revert AlreadyQueued(slot);\n\n        _slotQueued[slot] = true;\n        _queue.push(Pending({slot: slot, subtract: subtract, payTo: payTo, amount: amount}));\n\n        emit Queued(msg.sender, slot, subtract, _queue.length - 1);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Execute up to `max` parked interactions, in arrival order.\n    ///\n    /// @dev Permissionless on purpose. A parked withdrawal is somebody's money, and whether they\n    ///      get it back must not depend on a keeper choosing to finish its work.\n    function drainQueue(uint256 max) public returns (uint256 executed) {\n        uint256 end = _queue.length;\n        uint256 i = _drained;\n        uint256 stop = i + max;\n        if (stop > end) stop = end;\n\n        for (; i < stop; i++) {\n            Pending memory p = _queue[i];\n            _slotQueued[p.slot] = false;\n            // Marked done before it runs, not after. The execution ends in a token transfer, and\n            // an entry that is still marked pending while its transfer is in flight is an entry a\n            // re-entrant call could execute twice.\n            _drained = i + 1;\n            _execute(p.slot, p.amount, p.subtract, p.payTo);\n            executed++;\n        }\n\n        if (i == end && end != 0) {\n            delete _queue;\n            _drained = 0;\n        }\n\n        emit QueueDrained(executed);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev One page, inside `settle`.\n    function _drainQueue() internal {\n        drainQueue(DRAIN_PER_TX);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev The leaf is re-granted to its owner on every execution, not only on the call that\n    ///      queued it. `_update` replaces the ciphertexts it touches, and a handle nobody is\n    ///      allowed to decrypt is a balance its owner has lost sight of \u2014 the grant has to follow\n    ///      the write, wherever the write happens.\n    function _execute(uint32 slot, euint64 amount, bool subtract, address payTo) private {\n        uint32 period = currentPeriod();\n        _update(slot, amount, subtract, uint32(block.timestamp), period, periodStart(period));\n        _grantLeaf(slot, depositorAt[slot]);\n\n        if (payTo != address(0)) {\n            FHE.allowTransient(amount, address(token));\n            token.confidentialTransfer(payTo, amount);\n        }\n    }\n\n    function _requireSlot(address account) private view returns (uint32) {\n        if (!_hasSlot[account]) revert NoSlot(account);\n        return _slotOf[account];\n    }\n\n    // -------------------------------------------------------------- balances\n\n    function _balanceOf(uint32 slot) private view returns (euint64 balance, euint64 accrued) {\n        (euint64 a, euint64 b, , ) = _leaf(slot);\n        return (b, a);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The caller's principal, as a handle they are allowed to decrypt.\n    function confidentialBalanceOf(address account) external view returns (euint64) {\n        (euint64 balance, ) = _balanceOf(_slotOf[account]);\n        return balance;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The integral accrued so far this period, up to the last time this leaf moved.\n    ///\n    /// @dev Paired with `lastMoved`, this is everything the owner needs: the live weight is\n    ///      `accrued + balance * (now - lastMoved)`, and the elapsed term is public, so the owner\n    ///      finishes the calculation off chain after decrypting two handles.\n    function confidentialWeightOf(address account) external view returns (euint64) {\n        (, euint64 accrued) = _balanceOf(_slotOf[account]);\n        return accrued;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Seal the caller's own weight at this instant and grant it to them.\n    ///\n    /// @dev The pair of handles above is the cheap path \u2014 two reads and one multiplication the\n    ///      owner finishes in the clear. This is the exact path, and it has to be a transaction\n    ///      rather than a view because sealing is arithmetic on ciphertexts and arithmetic on\n    ///      ciphertexts writes.\n    ///\n    ///      It seals a *leaf*, never an internal node. A leaf is one depositor and discloses only\n    ///      what that depositor already knows; an internal node is a sum over other people, and\n    ///      the only internal value this contract ever lets out is the child index of a draw.\n    function sealWeight() external returns (euint64) {\n        uint32 slot = _requireSlot(msg.sender);\n        uint32 period = currentPeriod();\n\n        euint64 weight = _sealed(leafOffset + slot, uint32(block.timestamp), period, periodStart(period));\n        FHE.allow(weight, msg.sender);\n        _sealedWeight[msg.sender] = weight;\n\n        emit WeightSealed(msg.sender, slot, uint32(block.timestamp));\n        return weight;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The handle from the caller's last `sealWeight`, to decrypt under EIP-712.\n    function sealedWeightOf(address account) external view returns (euint64) {\n        return _sealedWeight[account];\n    }\n\n    /// @notice When this depositor's leaf last moved, and in which period.\n    function lastMoved(address account) external view returns (uint32 at, uint32 period) {\n        (, , uint32 lastUpdate, uint32 lastPeriod) = _leaf(_slotOf[account]);\n        return (lastUpdate, lastPeriod);\n    }\n}\n","keccak256":"0xf2a2ef70d1ccc2d06378290f190774e99d3ecbc725259e256eb1706f23f9ccf6","license":"MIT"},"contracts/WeightTree.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.27;\n\nimport {FHE, euint64} from \"@fhevm/solidity/lib/FHE.sol\";\nimport {ZamaEthereumConfig} from \"@fhevm/solidity/config/ZamaConfig.sol\";\n\nimport {Limits} from \"./Limits.sol\";\n\n/// @notice The core of Ticket: odds that are time-weighted, encrypted, and still summable.\n///\n/// @dev Odds cannot be \"balance at draw time\" \u2014 depositing a moment before the draw and leaving a\n///      moment after would be free money, and it is the exploit the whole design exists to close.\n///      So the quantity that decides a draw is the *integral of balance over the period*, and it\n///      has to be maintained under encryption, where you cannot look at a number to decide what to\n///      do next.\n///\n///      Each node keeps two ciphertexts and two plaintext timestamps:\n///\n///        A  accumulated integral for the current period, up to `lastUpdate`\n///        B  current total balance in this subtree\n///\n///      and the weight at any later time T is\n///\n///        weight(T) = A + B * (T - lastUpdate)\n///\n///      The multiplier is a *plaintext* elapsed time, so this is a ciphertext-by-scalar multiply \u2014\n///      one of the cheap operations \u2014 not the ciphertext-by-ciphertext multiply that would blow the\n///      per-transaction compute budget. Nothing about the balance is revealed by knowing how long\n///      it sat there.\n///\n///      `B` is additive across children by construction, and `A` is the integral of `B`, so a\n///      parent's pair is exactly the subtree's pair provided every change folds the whole path to\n///      the root before touching a balance. `_update` does that, which is why it walks upward.\n///      That is what makes the draw a descent over `depth` levels instead of a scan over `N`\n///      depositors.\n///\n///      Periods reset lazily. A node whose `lastPeriod` is stale has, by definition, an integral of\n///      zero for the current period; there is no O(N) reset pass, and there does not need to be.\nabstract contract WeightTree is ZamaEthereumConfig {\n    struct Node {\n        euint64 A;\n        euint64 B;\n        uint32 lastUpdate;\n        uint32 lastPeriod;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Children per node.\n    uint32 public immutable arity;\n\n    /// @notice Leaves, and therefore the maximum number of depositors.\n    uint32 public immutable capacity;\n\n    /// @notice Levels between the root and a leaf. The number of steps a draw takes.\n    uint8 public immutable treeDepth;\n\n    /// @notice Index of the leaf holding slot 0.\n    uint32 public immutable leafOffset;\n\n    mapping(uint32 index => Node node) internal _nodes;\n\n    error ArityOutOfRange(uint32 arity);\n    error CapacityNotAPowerOfArity(uint32 capacity, uint32 arity);\n    error CapacityTooLarge(uint32 capacity);\n\n    /// @param arity_ children per node\n    /// @param capacity_ leaf count, which must be an exact power of `arity_`\n    constructor(uint32 arity_, uint32 capacity_) {\n        if (arity_ < 2 || arity_ > 32) revert ArityOutOfRange(arity_);\n        if (capacity_ > Limits.MAX_SLOTS) revert CapacityTooLarge(capacity_);\n\n        // Walk the powers of the arity rather than trusting a log. `internalNodes` accumulates\n        // (k^d - 1) / (k - 1) on the way, which is the index the leaves start at.\n        uint32 size = 1;\n        uint32 internalNodes = 0;\n        uint8 d = 0;\n        while (size < capacity_) {\n            internalNodes += size;\n            size *= arity_;\n            d += 1;\n        }\n        if (size != capacity_) revert CapacityNotAPowerOfArity(capacity_, arity_);\n\n        arity = arity_;\n        capacity = capacity_;\n        treeDepth = d;\n        leafOffset = internalNodes;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Index of node `n`'s `j`-th child.\n    function childOf(uint32 n, uint32 j) public view returns (uint32) {\n        return n * arity + 1 + j;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Index of node `n`'s parent. Undefined at the root.\n    function parentOf(uint32 n) public view returns (uint32) {\n        return (n - 1) / arity;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The weight of a subtree at time `T`, without writing anything.\n    ///\n    /// @dev The period branch is on plaintext, not on a ciphertext: whether a node is stale is a\n    ///      property of block timestamps, which are public anyway. A stale node contributes only\n    ///      the balance it carried into the period.\n    function _sealed(uint32 n, uint32 T, uint32 period, uint32 periodStart) internal returns (euint64) {\n        Node storage node = _nodes[n];\n\n        euint64 weight;\n        if (node.lastPeriod != period) {\n            weight = FHE.mul(node.B, uint64(T - periodStart));\n        } else {\n            weight = FHE.add(node.A, FHE.mul(node.B, uint64(T - node.lastUpdate)));\n        }\n\n        FHE.allowThis(weight);\n        return weight;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Move a node into the current period, discarding the previous period's integral.\n    ///\n    /// @dev Odds are per-period, so last period's integral is not merely stale, it is wrong. The\n    ///      balance carries over; the integral does not.\n    function _roll(uint32 n, uint32 period, uint32 periodStart) internal {\n        Node storage node = _nodes[n];\n        if (node.lastPeriod == period) return;\n\n        node.A = FHE.asEuint64(0);\n        node.lastUpdate = periodStart;\n        node.lastPeriod = period;\n        FHE.allowThis(node.A);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Fold elapsed time into the integral, bringing `A` current as of `t`.\n    function _fold(uint32 n, uint32 t) internal {\n        Node storage node = _nodes[n];\n        uint32 elapsed = t - node.lastUpdate;\n        if (elapsed == 0) return;\n\n        node.A = FHE.add(node.A, FHE.mul(node.B, uint64(elapsed)));\n        node.lastUpdate = t;\n        FHE.allowThis(node.A);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Let `owner` decrypt their own leaf, and nothing above it.\n    ///\n    /// @dev A leaf is one depositor, so granting it discloses only what that depositor already\n    ///      knows. Internal nodes are sums over other people and are never granted to anyone \u2014\n    ///      the contract holds them and the KMS decrypts exactly one of them per draw level.\n    ///\n    ///      Both halves are granted because the weight is `A + B * (T - lastUpdate)` and the\n    ///      elapsed term is plaintext: the owner decrypts two numbers and finishes the arithmetic\n    ///      in the clear, which costs the chain nothing.\n    function _grantLeaf(uint32 slot, address owner) internal {\n        Node storage node = _nodes[leafOffset + slot];\n        FHE.allow(node.A, owner);\n        FHE.allow(node.B, owner);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice A leaf's stored halves, for the owner to decrypt.\n    function _leaf(uint32 slot) internal view returns (euint64 a, euint64 b, uint32 lastUpdate, uint32 lastPeriod) {\n        Node storage node = _nodes[leafOffset + slot];\n        return (node.A, node.B, node.lastUpdate, node.lastPeriod);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Apply a balance change at `slot` and carry it to the root.\n    ///\n    /// @dev Every node on the path is folded *before* its balance moves, which is what keeps `A`\n    ///      the true integral of `B` at every level. Off-path nodes are untouched and stay correct\n    ///      on their own terms \u2014 their balance did not change, so neither did their integral.\n    ///\n    /// @param slot the depositor's leaf\n    /// @param delta the amount, already clamped to `Limits.MAX_DEPOSIT`\n    /// @param subtract true for a withdrawal\n    function _update(\n        uint32 slot,\n        euint64 delta,\n        bool subtract,\n        uint32 t,\n        uint32 period,\n        uint32 periodStart\n    ) internal {\n        uint32 n = leafOffset + slot;\n\n        while (true) {\n            _roll(n, period, periodStart);\n            _fold(n, t);\n\n            Node storage node = _nodes[n];\n            node.B = subtract ? FHE.sub(node.B, delta) : FHE.add(node.B, delta);\n            FHE.allowThis(node.B);\n\n            if (n == 0) break;\n            n = parentOf(n);\n        }\n    }\n}\n","keccak256":"0x05e2cb58cda1d73d93d0606b05ed72103eb63bea9e4dd8624f59177ee798a57a","license":"MIT"},"encrypted-types/EncryptedTypes.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma devdoc.details: `FHE` cannot branch on a ciphertext and cannot index an array by one. Those two facts      are why every confidential lottery published so far walks all N depositors: the only      oblivious construction available is "compare the random point against every prefix sum".      The way out is an observation about what the leak actually is. A tournament descent that      publicly reveals which child it took at each level reveals the winner's slot index one      digit at a time — and the winner's identity is published anyway. The path *is* the      answer. Revealing it early costs nothing, and it turns an O(N) scan into a descent over      `treeDepth` levels.      Scaling the random point is the other half. Division by a ciphertext does not exist, and      rejection sampling would leak a bit about the pool total on every retry. So the test          r / 2^32  <  prefix_j / total      is cross-multiplied into          r * total  <  prefix_j * 2^32          (in euint128)      exact, unbiased to one part in 2^32, no division, and no total ever revealed. Descending      needs no fresh randomness: the residual `R' = R - prefix_{j-1} * 2^32` is uniform on      `[0, w_j * 2^32)`, so the same test recurses against the child's own prefix sums. There is      one ciphertext-by-ciphertext multiply in the entire draw — the most expensive operation      available, spent exactly once, at the root.      **Why a level is two transactions.** The binding per-transaction ceiling is sequential      depth, not global compute, which is the opposite of what the sizing arithmetic suggested.      Sealing the k children is k independent chains and is depth-flat at every arity; the      selection that follows is 77% of the depth budget on its own. Measured together they      revert. Split, they fit — see `bench/RESULTS.md` and `deploy/params.ts`.      A draw is therefore `1 + 2 * treeDepth + 1` transactions: commit (which seals the root's      children), then select and reveal at each level, then settle. Bounded, driven by a      keeper, and presented to a depositor as one action with a real progress state.

abandonDraw(uint256).details: Deliberately callable by anyone and deliberately not a keeper privilege. The failure      this exists for is the keeper going away, so a rescue only the keeper can perform is      not a rescue. It cannot be used to cancel a draw that is merely slow: the window is      six hours and a draw takes minutes.      No winner is paid and none is invented. The draw is recorded as abandoned at whatever      level it reached, which is a fact worth keeping on a page that claims verifiability.

commitDraw(uint64).details: The prize is plaintext and pulled from the sponsor here, not taken from the pool.      Depositors' principal is not a prize pool and paying out of it would silently make      this a lottery; the interface says "sponsor-funded" because the contract is.      `FHE.randEuint32` is a state-changing call — randomness cannot be produced by a      read-only call — which is one reason the commit is its own transaction rather than      something a viewer can simulate.

confidentialWeightOf(address).details: Paired with `lastMoved`, this is everything the owner needs: the live weight is      `accrued + balance * (now - lastMoved)`, and the elapsed term is public, so the owner      finishes the calculation off chain after decrypting two handles.

deposit(bytes32,bytes).details: The amount is clamped twice and neither clamp can revert, because reverting on an      encrypted comparison would leak the comparison. `FHE.min` caps it at `MAX_DEPOSIT` so      the aggregates cannot overflow, and the token itself caps it at the sender's balance      and returns what actually moved. That return value, not the request, is what enters      the tree — otherwise a depositor could claim odds on money they never sent.

drainQueue(uint256).details: Permissionless on purpose. A parked withdrawal is somebody's money, and whether they      get it back must not depend on a keeper choosing to finish its work.

revealLevel(uint256,bytes32[],uint8,byte.details: Two separate bindings have to hold and only one of them comes from the KMS.      `FHE.checkSignatures` proves the cleartext belongs to *these handles in this order*;      it says nothing about whether these handles are the ones this draw published. So the      handle is compared against stored state first. Without that check a valid proof for      any other publicly decryptable value would drive this draw wherever its holder liked.      The residual is computed here rather than at selection because the child index is      plaintext by now — which is what lets the prefix be summed over a known range in a      balanced tree, four operations deep instead of fifteen.

sealWeight().details: The pair of handles above is the cheap path — two reads and one multiplication the      owner finishes in the clear. This is the exact path, and it has to be a transaction      rather than a view because sealing is arithmetic on ciphertexts and arithmetic on      ciphertexts writes.      It seals a *leaf*, never an internal node. A leaf is one depositor and discloses only      what that depositor already knows; an internal node is a sum over other people, and      the only internal value this contract ever lets out is the child index of a draw.

selectLevel(uint256).details: The prefix sum is a Hillis-Steele scan rather than a running total. A running total is      a chain of k-1 sequential adds, and depth that grows with arity is exactly what makes      k=16 revert. The scan is log2(k) rounds deep at the cost of k*log2(k) additions — it      trades global compute, which is slack, for depth, which is not.      The published index is the count of prefix boundaries the point has passed. A child      with zero weight has the same prefix as the one before it, so the count skips it and      it can never be selected — no branch on a ciphertext required to exclude it.

settle(uint256).details: A draw that lands on an unoccupied leaf means the pool's total weight was zero — every      depositor had withdrawn before the seal. There is no way to detect that under      encryption and no reason to pretend otherwise: the prize goes back to the sponsor and      the event records a winner of `address(0)`.

withdraw(bytes32,bytes).details: Asking for more than you hold is not an error and must not be one: an error is a      public signal about a private balance. The request is silently clamped, which is both      the safe behaviour and the honest one — you cannot underflow the tree by guessing.

DRAW_TIMEOUT.details: A draw holds the tree still, and an unfinished draw holds it still forever. The KMS is      a live service and live services stop: if a published index never comes back, the pool      would be frozen with people's money in it and no way out. So a draw that has not      settled within this window can be abandoned by anybody, which releases the pool and      returns the sponsor's prize. Generously long, because abandoning a draw that was only      slow is worse than waiting.

_children.details: The sealed weights of the current node's children. Overwritten level by level; the      draw never needs a level it has already descended past.

_index.details: The published child index for the level currently awaiting reveal.

_point.details: The residual random point, scaled by 2^32. Set once at the root, narrowed on descent.

openDraw.details: Zero is not a live draw id, so `openDraw == 0` reads as "no draw in flight".

owner.details: Deliberately nothing else. The owner cannot pause the pool, cannot move a deposit,      cannot influence a draw and cannot reach the money — a depositor's withdrawal does not      depend on anybody's goodwill, which is the only reason a confidential pool is worth      trusting. Rotation exists because a keeper key that is lost or leaked would otherwise      end the pool's life: no key, no further draws, forever.

InvalidKMSSignatures().notice: Returned if the returned KMS signatures are not valid.

SenderNotAllowedToUseHandle(bytes32,addr.notice: Returned if the sender is not allowed to use the handle.

ZamaProtocolUnsupported().notice: Returned if the Zama protocol is not supported on the current chain

PublicDecryptionVerified(bytes32[],bytes.notice: This event is emitted when public decryption has been successfully verified.

DRAW_TIMEOUT().notice: How long a draw may sit unfinished before anyone may abandon it.

abandonDraw(uint256).notice: Release a draw that has stopped making progress, and give the prize back.

capacity().notice: Leaves, and therefore the maximum number of depositors.

commitDraw(uint64).notice: Open a draw, freeze the clock it will be judged against, and seal the root's         children in the same transaction.

confidentialBalanceOf(address).notice: The caller's principal, as a handle they are allowed to decrypt.

confidentialWeightOf(address).notice: The integral accrued so far this period, up to the last time this leaf moved.

deposit(bytes32,bytes).notice: Deposit an encrypted amount. The caller must have made this contract an operator         on the token first.

drainQueue(uint256).notice: Execute up to `max` parked interactions, in arrival order.

drawInFlight().notice: True while a draw holds the tree still. Deposits and withdrawals are queued rather         than blocked during this window — see `TicketPool._applyOrQueue`.

keeper().notice: Whoever may open a draw. Driving one forward is permissionless on purpose: a         half-finished draw holds the pool, so nobody should be able to strand it.

lastMoved(address).notice: When this depositor's leaf last moved, and in which period.

leafOffset().notice: Index of the leaf holding slot 0.

levelIndexHandle(uint256).notice: The published index handle for the level awaiting reveal, for the relayer to         publicly decrypt.

nextSlot().notice: Slots are assigned once and never reused, so this only ever climbs.

owner().notice: The only privilege in the contract: naming the keeper.

parentOf(uint32).notice: Index of node `n`'s parent. Undefined at the root.

participantCount().notice: Depositors who have ever deposited. The draw descends over `capacity` leaves         regardless, so this is a UX number, not a cost.

queueLength().notice: How many interactions are still waiting to be executed.

revealLevel(uint256,bytes32[],uint8,byte.notice: Submit the KMS-signed decryption of the published index, descend into that child,         and seal its children ready for the next level.

sealWeight().notice: Seal the caller's own weight at this instant and grant it to them.

sealedWeightOf(address).notice: The handle from the caller's last `sealWeight`, to decrypt under EIP-712.

selectLevel(uint256).notice: Scan the sealed children into prefix sums, drop the random point on them, and         publish which child it landed in.

setKeeper(address).notice: Name a new keeper. Cannot be done while a draw is in flight, so a rotation can         never orphan one halfway down the tree.

settle(uint256).notice: Pay the winner, release the tree, and execute everything that arrived mid-draw.

slotOf(address).notice: The caller's slot, and whether they have one at all.

treeDepth().notice: Levels between the root and a leaf. The number of steps a draw takes.

withdraw(bytes32,bytes).notice: Withdraw an encrypted amount, clamped to the caller's balance.

userdoc.notice: Picks one winner out of an encrypted pool without ever reading a balance.
